extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners (and practitioners) on applying the prior-art exception under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C)/102(c), handling related amendments (37 CFR 1.71(g)), double patenting issues, form paragraphs, affidavits/declarations, and required file-record practices such as search notes and claim indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g) (disclosure of JRA parties / timing and correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.71(g) permits an application to disclose or be amended to disclose the names of the parties to a joint research agreement to invoke the prior art exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) and 102(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification may be amended to disclose each party's name because 35 U.S.C. 102(c)(3) requires it. If an amendment under 1.71(g)(1) is not filed within certain time periods (within three months of national filing date; within three months of national stage entry for international apps; before mailing of first Office action on the merits; or before mailing of first Office action after RCE under 1.114), it must be accompanied by the processing fee per 1.17(i). If the amendment is filed after the issue fee is paid and the issued patent does not include the JRA names, the patent must be corrected by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 1.323 to make the amendment effective. The submission remains subject to rules of practice (e.g., 1.116, 1.121, 1.312); examiners may refuse entry if accompanied re-opening would necessitate terminal disclaimer entry (1.321(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for excepting subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter disclosed in a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO publication that is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) is only excepted when (A) a proper submission is filed establishing common ownership or a joint research agreement, (B) the reference only qualifies as prior art under 102(a)(2) (not 102(a)(1)), and (C) the reference was used in an anticipation rejection under 102(a)(2) or an obviousness rejection under 103 (not a double patenting rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 717.02(b) for establishing common ownership or a JRA; all three prongs (A,B,C) must be satisfied for the exception to apply. Note that a reference that is prior art under 102(a)(1) is not excepted even if it otherwise qualifies under 102(b)(2)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper submission to establish common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper submission to establish common ownership may be a clear and conspicuous statement that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed were, not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be conspicuous and identify the common assignee (see form paragraph notes). Failure to provide this required statement means the reference is not excepted under 102(b)(2)(C). Applicant may instead attempt to overcome a 102(a)(2) rejection via exceptions under 37 CFR 1.130(a) (obtained from inventor) or 1.130(b) (prior public disclosure affidavit/declaration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper submission to establish a joint research agreement (JRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper submission to establish a JRA may include (a) an amendment to the specification to disclose the names of the parties to the JRA (per 37 CFR 1.71(g)), and (b) a clear and conspicuous statement that the subject matter in the prior art was developed and the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of one or more parties to a JRA which was in effect on or before the effective filing date of the claimed invention, and that the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the JRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to supply the required amendment or statement (e.g., missing names or proof that the JRA was in effect by the effective filing date, or that the invention was made within the scope of the JRA), the attempt to except the reference is ineffective and examiner should use the form paragraph addressing missing requirements (see ¶7.20.05.aia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when common ownership or JRA not established
rubrics_metrics.description: If the file does not establish that the subject matter disclosed in the reference is excepted under 102(b)(2)(C), the examiner will (A) assume the subject matter is not excepted, (B) examine on all grounds other than any possible exception arising from 102(a)(2), (C) consider applicability of references under 102(a)(2) or 103 based on 102(a)(2), and (D) apply the best references against the claimed invention by rejections under 102 and 103 until the subject matter is shown to be excepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying disclosures that only qualify as prior art under 102(a)(2), the examiner should anticipate that the subject matter may later be shown excepted and consider alternative rejections. If an applied disclosure is later properly excepted and claims are not amended, the examiner generally may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made (except as provided in MPEP §706.07(a) and this section). If excepted subject matter gives rise to a new double patenting rejection necessitated by applicant amendment, that Office action may be made final provided no other new ground of rejection was introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when common ownership or JRA established
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application has established that the disclosure is excepted as prior art under 102(b)(2)(C), the examiner will (A) examine as to all grounds except the disclosure excepted as prior art under 102(a)(2), (B) examine for double patenting (statutory and nonstatutory) and make a provisional rejection if appropriate, and (C) invite applicant to file a terminal disclaimer to overcome provisional or actual nonstatutory double patenting rejections (see 37 CFR 1.321).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the excepted disclosure as if commonly owned for double patenting purposes. Use MPEP § 804 guidance for double patenting practice and 37 CFR 1.321 for terminal disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting rejections and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly owned applications of different inventive entities may be rejected for double patenting, and excepted subject matter under 102(b)(2)(C)/102(c) is treated as if commonly owned for double patenting analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting rejections can be provisional (based on a pending U.S. application) or actual. Nonstatutory double patenting rejections may be obviated by filing a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321, including language that the patent is enforceable only while commonly owned with the reference. Terminal disclaimers cannot overcome statutory double patenting. See MPEP §§ 804 and 804.02 for detailed guidance; treatment is analogous to CREATE Act situations and may require 1.321(d) compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.01.aia — 103 Rejection Using Prior Art Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) Because Reference is Prior Art Under 102(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph to be used when a reference that has been excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) nevertheless remains applicable as prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that applicant provided a submission claiming common ownership or JRA, but although subject matter in the reference has been excepted under 102(a)(2), it is still applicable as prior art under 102(a)(1). Applicant may overcome the 102(a)(1) rejection by a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the reference was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor (so not prior art under 102(b)(1)(A)), or under 1.130(b) by evidence of a prior public disclosure. Examiner notes: use only in apps filed on/after March 16, 2013, must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia, include identification instructions for bracketed fields (common assignee, the reference), and use following specified paragraphs when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.02.aia — Joint Inventors, Common Ownership Presumed
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph stating that an application currently names joint inventors and the examiner presumes claims' subject matter was commonly owned at the effective filing time absent evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises applicant of obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and effective filing dates of any claim not commonly owned so that examiner may consider applicability of 102(b)(2)(C). Examiner notes: use only in apps filed on/after March 16, 2013 where claims examined under AIA 102/103; must be preceded by 7.03.aia; use in all applications with joint inventors unless claims are clearly restricted to a single claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.04.aia — 102/103 Rejection Using 102(a)(2) Attempted Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) via Common Ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph to be used when applicant attempted to show the reference is excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) via common ownership but failed to provide a conspicuous statement that the claimed invention and the subject matter were owned by (or subject to assignment to) the same person no later than the effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States applicant must file the required submission to properly except the subject matter. Also suggests applicant may rely on 37 CFR 1.130(a)/(b) exceptions instead. Examiner notes: use only in apps filed on/after March 16, 2013 where AIA 102/103 applies; include identification instructions for bracketed fields (reference; common assignee); include this paragraph in all actions containing rejections using 102(a)(2) where an attempt to except was made but missing the required statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.05.aia — 102/103 Rejection Using 102(a)(2) Attempted Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) via JRA Provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph to be used when applicant attempted to except subject matter via the joint research agreement provisions but failed to supply required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructs that applicant must file the missing requirements (see 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) and 1.104(c)(4)(ii)). Advises alternative routes under 37 CFR 1.130(a)/(b) to overcome the rejection. Examiner notes: use only in apps filed on/after March 16, 2013 where AIA 102/103 applies; include this paragraph in all obviousness or anticipation rejections where an attempt to except via JRA was ineffective; bracket fields should identify reference and reason(s) why attempt is ineffective (e.g., noncompliance with statute or rule). Suggests use of form paragraph 7.38.01 or 7.38.02 where submission is persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131(c) — Affidavit or declaration to disqualify commonly owned patent as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103 in view of a U.S. patent or publication that is not prior art under pre-AIA 102(b), and the inventions are not patentably distinct and are owned by the same party, the applicant/patent owner may disqualify the patent/publication as prior art by submitting (1) a terminal disclaimer per 1.321(c), and (2) an oath/declaration that the application/patent under reexamination and the reference are currently owned by the same party and that the inventor named is the prior inventor under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision applies to applications/patents with claims having effective filing dates before March 16, 2013 (with specific cross-reference date rules). The affidavit/declaration may be signed by inventor(s), attorney/agent of record, or assignee(s) of entire interest. Terminal disclaimers only overcome nonstatutory double patenting; cannot be used for statutory double patenting. The phrase 'prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104 as in effect on March 15, 2013' carries limitations on where a date of invention can be established (NAFTA/WTO date limits). A U.S. patent or publication that anticipates the claimed subject matter cannot be disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c) or 1.131(c). See MPEP §§ 804.03 and 2146-2146.03 for related subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Wrapper as official record (MPEP § 719 — Papers in Image File Wrapper)
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic file record (image file wrapper) maintained by the Office is the official record of the application; papers that do not become a permanent part of the record should not be entered as papers in the image file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No paper legally entered should ever be withdrawn or expunged without Director's special authority. 37 CFR 1.59 provides limited expungement for unintentionally submitted documents or proprietary information not relevant to patentability. Use form paragraph 7.214 to notify applicant that papers ordinarily will not be returned; Office will furnish copies at applicant's expense per 1.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence of inventor changed (MPEP § 719.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish 'residence' from 'mailing address'. Unless specifically requested by applicant, the residence(s) associated with inventor(s) will not be changed in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If revised residence information is to appear in a patent application publication, revised information must be entered into Office electronic records at least nine weeks before publication date. For patent applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, for a patent to issue with new residence applicants must file a corrected Application Data Sheet (37 CFR 1.76(c)) with underlining for insertions and strike-through/brackets for removals. For apps filed prior to Sept 16, 2012, applicants are encouraged to file a Supplemental ADS showing new information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification during examination (MPEP § 719.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is received in a Technology Center, the classification of the application and the initials/name of the examiner or other assigned docket designation are noted in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 909.01(b) for additional classification/docketing practice. This is part of maintaining proper file record of assignment and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index of Claims (MPEP § 719.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Index of Claims in the image file wrapper should be updated with each Office action to maintain a reliable index of all claims in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim numbers refer to claim numbering during prosecution; adjacent columns refer to status of each claim and final column to final numbering of allowed claims. Examiners should record dates of Office actions and resulting status for each claim; at allowance, examiner places final patent claim numbers in the 'Final' column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Search requirements and recording (MPEP § 719.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits, the examiner must record in the Official Correspondence 'Search Notes' form the areas searched, dates of search, and examiner initials. In subsequent actions where search is updated or further search is made, the examiner must indicate updates, additional fields searched, dates, and initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any search updates should include the databases and the search queries/classifications used in the original search. Include appropriate search history printouts in the application file anytime a limited electronic search was performed. The record aids evaluation of patent strength/validity, particularly in litigation. Searches are listed in the 'SEARCHED' boxes and/or 'SEARCH NOTES' box of the Search Notes form. Great care should be taken to clearly indicate what was searched and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries in 'SEARCHED' boxes — format (MPEP § 719.05.I.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Search Notes form includes three 'SEARCHED' boxes for recording searches in Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC), CPC Combination Sets and U.S. Patent Classification (USPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting a classification search, ensure the proper SEARCHED box(es) is/are used. For CPC classification searches, indicate how the search was limited (e.g., which CPC symbols and any limitations). If absence of entries appears for some classification symbols, it should indicate either all documents with those symbols were reviewed or a search history printout is in the file indicating how that search was limited. A complete search history printout must be included whenever a limited electronic search was conducted.
